page: Microsoft Azure E8ps_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the ARM64 processor architecture and running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Storage architecture for this instance relies entirely on external disks, as no local storage is bundled with the host hardware. It supports Azure Premium Storage to meet persistent disk requirements. In terms of networking, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly by default.

By employing power-efficient ARM64 computing cores alongside an elevated 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, the E8ps_v7 offers favorable operational cost efficiency for RAM-heavy enterprise applications. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral storage, which requires all disk transactions to rely on network-attached storage options. Workloads best aligned with the hardware profile include in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise backend services.
